title: The Road to Explainability is Paved with Bias: Measuring the Fairness of Explanations
findings: The paper contains no findings related to religion, as it was not a variable of study. The key findings are that the fidelity of explanations varies significantly between subgroups based on race and sex, and that robust training methods can reduce but not eliminate these gaps.

measurement_description: The paper does not measure anything related to faith or religion. The benchmark measures the fairness of post-hoc explainability methods by evaluating 'fidelity gaps' between different protected subgroups defined by sex and race.
